dim_1_core_thesis.premise: Relational mind games are intentional or recurring manipulative behaviors where one partner exploits the other's emotions, attention, and uncertainty to establish power, asymmetric control, and unilateral validation within the dynamic.
dim_1_core_thesis.paradigm_shift: Conventional intuition often misinterprets coldness, delayed responses, and mixed signals as cute shyness, playing hard to get, or signs that a partner is simply upset and needs more pursuit. In reality, persistent asymmetric initiation, feigned nonchalance, backhanded insults (negging), artificial scarcity threats, weaponized silent treatment, and manufactured jealousy are structural power dynamics designed to erode the partner's self-esteem and induce desperate pursuit.

dim_2_causal_model.mechanism: The Mind Game Escalation Loop: Unilateral Withdrawal / Neg / Scarcity Signal -> Induction of Uncertainty & Fear of Loss in Partner -> Accelerated Desperation & Over-Pursuit (200% effort, gifts, compliments) -> Confirmation of Asymmetric Power & Validation Extraction -> Deepened Hierarchy & Depleted Self-Respect.
dim_2_causal_model.ratios_in_prose: The Over-Pursuit Effort Inversion: when an individual supplies 200% of the initiation, emotional labor, and reassurance while their partner supplies 0%, the resulting dynamic produces exhaustion and anxiety rather than relational security.

dim_3_master_analogy.analogy: The Casino Slot Machine (Intermittent Reinforcement Trap): Mind games function precisely like a slot machine. If the player won every pull or lost every pull reliably, they would walk away. By alternating feigned indifference ('I don't even care'), scarcity threats ('my ex still texts me'), and sudden crumb rewards, the manipulator keeps the partner emotionally hooked, frantically pulling the lever of validation at increasing personal cost.

classifications.etiology: Deliberate chipping away of the partner's self-worth so they feel lucky to receive attention.

classifications.symptom: Flaunting alternative romantic options or ex-partners ('my ex still texts me') to manufacture fear of replacement.
classifications.etiology: Creating an artificial sense of high demand to monopolize the partner's focus and effort.

classifications.symptom: Prolonged, stonewalling silence used as punishment and emotional abuse rather than a temporary cooling-off period followed by repair.
classifications.etiology: Exerting dominance by stripping the partner of voice, resolution, and emotional safety.

classifications.symptom: Openly boasting about giving numbers to strangers or being pursued by others to test the partner's emotional reactivity.
classifications.etiology: Extracting jealous distress as proof of value and dominance.

failure_modes: Retaliatory Mind Games: Attempting to 'counter-game' a manipulative partner by playing cold, which simply escalates toxicity and compromises integrity.
Over-Explaining and Begging: Trying to logically debate or persuade a manipulator into showing care, which feeds their validation.
Confusing Abuse with Affection: Believing that intense jealousy tests and silent treatments are evidence of passionate love rather than control.

algorithm: 1. Identify the Pattern: Differentiate a temporary bad mood from repeated, structural mind games over time.
2. Break the Desperation Loop: Cease reactive chasing, excessive texting, and panic-driven reassurance seeking when faced with coldness.
3. Enforce Equal Initiation: Step back from unilateral initiation; allow the other person space to reach out, miss you, and plan dates.
4. Neutralize Negging Instantly: Do not accept backhanded compliments; maintain unwavering certainty in your intrinsic worth.
5. Refuse Triangulation & Manufactured Jealousy: Respond with calm neutrality ('If you feel they are a better match, you should pursue them') and walk away.
6. Establish Self-Respect as Non-Negotiable: Never trade personal dignity to keep someone in your life.

ai_generated_practical_applications: The Initiation Audit: Count who initiates communication over a 7-day span. If initiation is 100% unilateral, pause initiation to test for organic reciprocity.
The Calm Non-Reactivity Stance: When confronted with manufactured jealousy or scarcity claims, do not display frantic anxiety. Offer calm release without competition.
The Exit Boundary: If silent treatment or negging persists as a chronic dynamic, prioritize self-respect and walk away cleanly.

dim_6_skeptic_box.pop_culture_distortion: Dating culture often normalizes games like 'the 3-day rule', playing aloof, or making partners jealous as exciting romantic courtship or harmless playful tension.
dim_6_skeptic_box.clinical_empirical_reality: In interpersonal psychology, sustained manipulation of attention and uncertainty triggers attachment distress, somatic anxiety, and trauma bonding. Healthy attachment thrives on predictability, mutual initiation, and direct communication. When mind games become chronic, they transition from awkward dating behavior into emotional abuse.

proposed_concepts.name: Asymmetric Initiation Pattern
proposed_concepts.definition: A relational pattern wherein one partner deliberately refrains from ever initiating text messages, phone calls, or date plans, forcing the other partner to sustain all relational momentum.

proposed_concepts.name: Negging Dynamics
proposed_concepts.definition: A manipulative tactic involving backhanded compliments and deliberate status-undermining remarks designed to erode a partner's self-esteem and create an artificial power imbalance.

proposed_concepts.name: Relational Scarcity Tactics
proposed_concepts.definition: The deliberate manufacturing of perceived competition—such as boasting of external options or past exes—to induce fear of replacement and provoke unilateral over-investment.

proposed_concepts.name: Prolonged Silent Treatment
proposed_concepts.definition: The weaponized withdrawal of verbal contact and refusal to engage in conflict resolution, serving as emotional punishment and control rather than a constructive cooling-off period.

proposed_concepts.name: Manufactured Jealousy
proposed_concepts.definition: The intentional elicitation of jealousy through overt disclosures of outside romantic interest to test a partner's emotional compliance, dependency, and distress.

proposed_relationships.description: Negging and status erosion trigger the over-pursuit loop as the victim scrambles to regain approval.
Relational scarcity tactics activate the anxious attachment system through perceived threat of abandonment.
Prolonged silent treatment induces panic and frantic repair attempts in the anxious partner.
Manufactured jealousy and relational scarcity tactics are co-occurring mechanisms of manipulative control.
